one: In North Dakota, ask for your ballot by Monday, November 2, 2026.In North Dakota, the last day to ask for a mail ballot was Monday, November 2, 2026: you can still vote in person, early or on Election Day.In North Dakota, the last day to ask for a mail ballot was Monday, November 2, 2026: you can still vote in person on Election Day.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in North Dakota, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Monday, November 2Passed

There is no fixed date. State law says to send your application early enough to receive, mark and mail the ballot before Election Day. The auditor cannot hand out absentee ballots on Election Day except in an emergency, so the practical last day is Monday, November 2, 2026. (the law)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be received by the county auditor before the polls close on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A ballot that arrives later is not counted with the others. (the law)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Monday, November 2, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on North Dakota’s own site

At school away from home, in North Dakota or in another state? What North Dakota says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. State law says any qualified voter may vote an absentee ballot. North Dakota has no voter registration; you prove who you are and where you live with your ID. (the law)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Fill out the absentee ballot application form on the Secretary of State's site, then print it, sign it and send it to your county auditor. The application asks for your ID information, which is checked against the voter record. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Get an application from your county auditor (or the Secretary of State), fill it out, sign it and return it to the county auditor by mail, fax, email or in person. In counties that vote by mail, the county auditor mails every voting-age resident an application (not a ballot); you return it to get a ballot. (official page)
  • In person. Take your application to your county auditor's office. If an emergency keeps you from voting in person on Election Day, an agent can get a ballot for you that day; it must be back at the auditor's office by 4 p.m. on Election Day. (the law)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it back by U.S. mail; you pay the postage. It must arrive before the polls close on Election Day. (official page)
  • Drop box. The Secretary of State says secure absentee ballot drop boxes are provided in each county; check its county drop box list for yours. Put your ballot in by the time the polls close on Election Day. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Hand it to your county auditor before the polls close on Election Day. Absentee ballots are NOT accepted at polling places on Election Day. (official page)

What the envelope needs

No witness or notary is needed. Your application must give valid ID information (a North Dakota driver's license or non-driver ID, a Tribal ID or letter, or a long-term care certificate). If your ID does not show your current address, include a copy of a document that does. You sign the statement on the return envelope swearing where you live; that signature is compared with the one on your application, so only you should sign it. (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on North Dakota’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 19, 2026 to Monday, November 2, 2026.

Counties that choose to offer early voting hold it during the 15 days before the election (from Monday, October 19 through Monday, November 2, 2026), on business days and hours set by the county auditor. Not every county offers it; check your county auditor. (the law)

Students

At school in North Dakota, away from home

The Secretary of State says a North Dakota student at college elsewhere in the state can vote with either their home address or their college address. To use the home address, you vote in that county with an ID showing it. To use the college address, update your North Dakota ID, or show your ID plus your student ID and a printed letter from the school with your address, or your ID plus a bill or bank statement with your current address. To vote absentee, ask the county auditor of the county for the address you are voting with. (official page)

At school in another state, with North Dakota as home

The Secretary of State's pages speak to students from other states at North Dakota schools, not to North Dakotans at school elsewhere. State law says you have only one residence, the place you return to when away for work or other temporary purposes, and you keep your North Dakota residence until you gain another. A North Dakota student at school in another state can ask their county auditor for an absentee ballot. (the law)

Military and overseas

Military members, their spouses and dependents, and North Dakotans living outside the U.S. apply through the Secretary of State's site and can get the ballot by email, fax or mail. Ballots go out 46 days before the election; later requests are filled within 2 business days. A military ID or U.S. passport works as ID for this application. The ballot must be mailed or sent electronically by the close of polls on Election Day. If yours does not come, you can use the Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot. (official page)

North Dakota in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • If you voted by absentee ballot, state law says you may not also vote in person at the same election.
  • If you asked in your June primary application for a November ballot too, the Secretary of State says it is mailed at the beginning of October.
  • Students from other states at North Dakota schools: the Secretary of State says they vote absentee or in person in their home state, unless they switch to a North Dakota ID, which makes North Dakota their residence (and may affect financial aid tied to residence elsewhere).
  • We did not check North Dakota's poll hours, so this record says 'before the polls close' rather than a clock time; ask your county auditor.
  • That an application can be sent by fax or email comes from state law 16.1-07-05 (source 2).
  • That North Dakota has no voter registration comes from the Secretary of State's Voting in North Dakota page (source 9).

How this was checked

  • The FVAP page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.

polls:
Polls open between 7 and 9 a.m. and close between 7 and 9 p.m. local time; each county or city sets the hours. (the law)

  • rest of the state: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. CST
  • The southwest: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. MST

Anyone in line when the polls close may still vote.
